reason: Python's argparse took prog from the invoked script (tools/<tool>.py); the Go binaries are run as their installed command (tools/install.sh), so usage and help name that command, not a retired .py script.

usage: bogcycles [-h] [--json] bog

bog-cycles: potential feedback loops in a station config.bog link graph (B1189-G3 / B1191-G3).

N4 logic is event-driven (no execution order): a link cycle can oscillate or storm actions (B6/B538). This tool
reads the bog with the bog-nav model (tools/bognav: the same parser, SlotPath name decoding and parse cache),
builds the COMPONENT-level directed graph from the saved links (`b:Link` / `b:ConversionLink` are children of
the TARGET; `sourceOrd = h:<source handle>`) and reports strongly connected components of size > 1 and
self-loops. Each cycle lists the slot-level link edges that form it (`/A.out -> /B.in`): the links whose
source and target components are both in the cycle. It is a conservative CANDIDATE list for a human:
legitimate feedback (PID, hysteresis) also appears. Dangling `h:` references are reported (a link with an
unresolvable source creates no knob and no fault, B1115); a non-handle sourceOrd (`station:|slot:/...`)
is not an edge.
Usage: bogcycles <config.bog|backup.dist|file.xml> [--json]
Paths always start with `/` at the station root: `/Services/X`; an unnamed root (every station bog) is `/`,
a named root R renders as `/R` and its children as `/R/A`.
`links` counts the links whose source resolves (or is not a handle); a dangling link is counted in
`dangling` only. A missing slot name prints as `-` (null in --json).
Exit 1 if cycles found, 0 otherwise, 2 on a missing/unreadable/non-BOG or not well-formed XML input or
bad usage. Read-only, stdlib.

positional arguments:
  bog         config.bog, a .dist station backup or a plain BOG file.xml

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      machine JSON output
